record_type_quote:
In the current study, we sought to replicate main findings of
Melka et al. (2012)
that SNPs on three genes (rs16933812 on
PAX5
, rs7638110 on
MRPS22
, and rs9930333 on
FTO
) are associated with both BMI and SBP. We used data from the Nicotine Dependence In Teens (NDIT) study (
O’Loughlin et al., 2014
), a longitudinal investigation of adolescents in Montreal, Quebec, Canada followed from age 12 to 24 (i.e., from 1999 to 2012). The NDIT sample was similar in age and geographic location to SYS.

targets.authors: Melka M. G., Bernard M., Mahboubi A., Abrahamowicz M., Paterson A. D., Syme C., et al.
targets.title: Genome-wide scan for loci of adolescent obesity and their relationship with blood pressure

that SNPs on three genes (rs16933812 on

targets.outcome_quote:
In conclusion, we replicated two associations observed in an earlier study of Quebec adolescents of European ancestry between SNPs in the well-established adiposity genes
FTO
and
MTCH2
and BMI. However, we could not replicate SNPs at genes
PAX5
,
MRPS22
, or
MC4R
. None of the SNPs showed an association with SBP.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The concluding account explicitly reports replicated BMI associations and other associations that did not replicate; the shared BMI/SBP hypothesis is unsupported.

reasoning: Independent NDIT adolescent sample re-tests SYS findings. The GWAS and cohort references supply context or variants rather than additional explicitly targeted papers.
